SP recognized the change, returned the stick to the neutral to slightly aft position, held power only as high as required and completed the verification while continuing to clear outside. No IP intervention was required.
texts.3: SP ensured the area immediately in front of and behind the aircraft was clear, kept the control stick in the neutral to slightly aft position and advanced power smoothly and slowly only as high as required to verify proper function of the overspeed governor. SP cleared outside the aircraft throughout the check and the aircraft remained stationary. The pilot not flying guarded the brakes but had nothing to assume.
texts.4: SP executed an exceptional overspeed governor check, clearing ahead of and behind the aircraft before any power was applied and advancing the power lever so smoothly that the verification was obtained at the lowest usable setting. The stick was held neutral to slightly aft throughout, the nose gear strut did not compress and the outside scan was maintained without interrupting the parameter check. Departures from the prescribed technique were negligible.
texts.marginal: SP completed the overspeed governor check within standards, but power was advanced higher than the verification required and clearing outside was done once at the start rather than throughout. The trend is toward a check that stays safe because the ramp happened to remain empty. SP is expected to advance power only as far as needed and keep clearing outside for the duration of the run up.

texts_at.1: SP executed the overspeed governor check to the level expected at this stage, keeping the aircraft stationary and clearing outside, due to the aft stick pressure relaxing slightly as power came up and the nose gear strut beginning to compress before the stick was returned to neutral to slightly aft. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to hold the stick position fixed through the whole power application rather than letting it relax as power builds.
texts_at.2: SP completed the verification with the aircraft stationary and the outside scan maintained, due to the aft stick pressure relaxing as the power came up, which SP recognized and corrected before the check was called complete. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to set the stick position once at the start of the check and hold it fixed rather than resetting it partway through.
texts_at.3: SP kept the control stick neutral to slightly aft and cleared outside the aircraft throughout the check, due to power being held a moment longer than the verification strictly required before it was reduced. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to reduce power as soon as the verification is obtained rather than a moment after.

texts_above.2: SP recognized the nose gear strut beginning to compress as the aft stick pressure relaxed with the power increase, returned the stick to neutral to slightly aft, held power only as high as required and completed the verification while continuing to clear outside. Holding the stick position fixed through the whole power application, rather than resetting it once compression appears, would remove the correction from the check. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to solid overspeed governor check technique.
texts_above.3: SP cleared ahead of and behind the aircraft before any power was applied and advanced the power lever so smoothly that the verification was obtained at the lowest usable setting, with the stick held neutral to slightly aft throughout. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to well-developed overspeed governor check technique.
texts_above.4: SP cleared the aircraft before any power was applied and obtained the verification at the lowest usable setting with the stick held neutral to slightly aft and the outside scan uninterrupted throughout. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to outstanding overspeed governor check technique.

error_modes.label: BEFORE TAKEOFF CHECKS AND LINE UP CHAIN OF ACTIONS, TOLD REVIEW
error_modes.source: technique:3.11 BEFORE TAKEOFF AND LINEUP CHECKS

texts.0: SP, due to executing the Before Takeoff Checks early and then filling the wait with other procedures, ran a navigation setup and a fuel check between the Before Takeoff Checks and Line Up and broke the prescribed chain of actions. The takeoff and landing data were never reviewed against reported conditions that differed significantly from the forecast. IP had to stop the line up, recompute the data using actual conditions and rerun the Before Takeoff Checks.
texts.1: SP, due to treating the Before Takeoff Checks as one more item in the taxi flow, completed them well before the hold and inserted a radio and instrument check before requesting line up. SP reviewed the takeoff and landing data only after IP asked whether the reported wind and temperature had changed. The sequence held at the lower limit of the standard through IP prompting.
texts.2: SP, due to starting the Before Takeoff Checks too early at the hold, began an additional systems check while waiting for the line up clearance. SP recognized that the chain of actions had been broken, stopped the additional check, repeated the Before Takeoff Checks immediately before requesting line up and confirmed the takeoff and landing data against the reported conditions. The sequence was restored without IP intervention.
texts.3: SP reviewed the takeoff and landing data and confirmed them against the reported conditions before reaching the hold. The Before Takeoff Checks were executed last, right before Line Up, with no other checks or procedures executed between them, and the chain of Before Takeoff Checks, request for line up and line up was followed exactly. No item required prompting.
texts.4: SP reviewed the takeoff and landing data early, noted that the reported conditions were significantly different than forecast and recomputed using actual conditions before reaching the hold. The Before Takeoff Checks were then executed last and uninterrupted, the line up request followed immediately and the aircraft was lined up with the recomputed figures already passed to IP. Deviations from the prescribed chain of actions were negligible.
texts.marginal: SP kept the Before Takeoff Checks and Line Up in the prescribed order and reviewed the takeoff and landing data within standards, but the review was a glance at the briefed figures rather than a comparison with reported conditions. The trend is toward carrying forecast numbers into a takeoff executed in different actual conditions. SP is expected to compare reported wind, temperature and runway state against the briefed data and recompute when they differ significantly.

texts_at.1: SP reviewed the takeoff and landing data and executed the Before Takeoff Checks to the level expected at this stage, due to the checks being completed slightly ahead of the hold with one additional radio and instrument check inserted before line up was requested, breaking the prescribed chain by a single item. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to hold the Before Takeoff Checks until immediately before the line up request, with nothing inserted between them.
texts_at.2: SP repeated the Before Takeoff Checks immediately before requesting line up and confirmed the takeoff and landing data against the reported conditions, due to an additional systems check started while waiting for the line up clearance that broke the prescribed chain of actions before it was stopped and the sequence restored. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to hold at the hold-short line without starting any additional check once the Before Takeoff Checks are complete.
texts_at.3: SP reviewed the takeoff and landing data against the reported conditions and executed the Before Takeoff Checks last, right before Line Up, due to the review being a comparison against the briefed figures made a short interval before the hold rather than at the hold itself. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to make the comparison at the hold itself so it reflects the most current conditions available.

texts_above.2: SP recognized that the chain of actions had been broken by an additional systems check started while waiting for the line up clearance, stopped the check, repeated the Before Takeoff Checks immediately before requesting line up and confirmed the takeoff and landing data against the reported conditions. Holding at the hold-short line without starting any additional check once the Before Takeoff Checks are complete would remove the break from the chain entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to steady chain-of-actions discipline.
texts_above.3: SP reviewed the takeoff and landing data early, noted that the reported conditions were significantly different from the forecast and recomputed using actual conditions before reaching the hold, with the Before Takeoff Checks executed last and uninterrupted. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to consistently accurate takeoff-data review.
texts_above.4: SP recomputed the takeoff and landing data against actual conditions before reaching the hold and executed the Before Takeoff Checks last and uninterrupted, with the recomputed figures already passed to IP before line up. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exemplary chain-of-actions discipline.
